top_stories.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
top_stories.one_liner: In the Vals AI benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak hits 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks. Worse, the open-weight model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost.
top_stories.summary: In the Vals AI benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak hits 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks. Worse, the open-weight model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost.
top_stories.ai_overview: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking AI agents can break into realistic corporate networks on their own, Vals AI finds The Vals CyberOffense benchmark simulates realistic corporate networks to test this. Each agent operates solo on an isolated attack machine, starting with nothing but a public web address and zero human help.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: GPT-6 Sol, part of OpenAI's restricted Daybreak cyber program, posted the best result at 80.8 percent of objectives.
ai_key_details: Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017, a freely available open-weight model, isn't far behind at 72.8 percent and costs only about $3 per run instead of roughly $22.
Once a model's weights are public, no provider can control or restrict how it's used, Vals researchers say.
Deepseek scored zero results in its first 25 million tokens and made most of its progress only after 100 million tokens.

top_stories.ai_overview: Ripple-65B Preview delivers strong agentic coding results as a fully Apache 2.0 open US model AI chip design firm Ricursive Intelligence has trained an open language model.
